questions.q: What is Snowflake's VARIANT type designed to hold?
options: Semi-structured data such as JSON, Avro, and Parquet, natively in a single column
Only plain integers with variable precision
A reference to an external file on disk
A fixed-shape structured row type, like a user-defined table type
questions.explain: VARIANT is Snowflake's native type for semi-structured data, letting a column hold JSON, Avro, Parquet, and similar data without a fixed predeclared shape.

questions.q: What does T-SQL's closest equivalent to VARIANT actually look like structurally?
options: JSON stored as plain text in an NVARCHAR column, read with separate JSON functions
T-SQL stores JSON in a dedicated JSON binary type
T-SQL has a native VARIANT type identical to Snowflake's
T-SQL has no way to store JSON at all
questions.explain: T-SQL's JSON support (JSON_VALUE, JSON_QUERY, OPENJSON) operates on JSON text stored in an ordinary NVARCHAR column — the JSON is still just a string to the type system, unlike Snowflake's native VARIANT.

questions.q: In 'payload:user.name', what does the colon do?
options: Starts the path into the VARIANT value's fields
Casts the result to a STRING
Is just a typo-tolerant alias for a dot
Separates two different VARIANT columns
questions.explain: The colon begins a path into a VARIANT column; dots and brackets chain further down from there to reach nested fields.

questions.q: What does the :: operator do when extracting a value from a VARIANT path?
options: Casts the extracted value to a specific scalar type, such as STRING or NUMBER
Starts a new path into a nested VARIANT
Converts a string into JSON
Deletes a key from the VARIANT object
questions.explain: A value pulled from a VARIANT path is itself still a VARIANT until cast with :: to a real scalar type like STRING or NUMBER.

options: Casts a NUMBER to a STRING
Validates that a string is syntactically valid SQL
Converts a VARIANT value back into a JSON string
Converts a JSON string into a VARIANT value
questions.explain: PARSE_JSON() takes a JSON-formatted string and produces a VARIANT value that can then be queried with dot/bracket path notation.
